analysis:
Both changed files are test-only, so no production code, trust boundary, or key/attestation path changes in the supplied evidence.

LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift (head lines 181-207) adds forwardsServingStallRollbacksToProviderJob. It asserts three rollback env keys are in LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys and are not in WatchdogAgent.passthroughEnvKeys. The keys are GlobalKVCacheBudget.idleCacheSweepEnvironmentKey, EngineV2Factory.segmentRetentionEnvironmentKey and EngineV2Factory.segmentHostZerosEnvironmentKey. It also checks that unrelated secrets are excluded and that defaults stay enabled. This reinforces the allowlist-only env passthrough: UNRELATED_SECRET is filtered, and the watchdog is not given inference knobs. It does not widen what is forwarded to the plist.

StartupPreloadTests.swift (patch hunks at ~96, ~193, ~610) adds a ReclaimableMemory helper and two tests. One checks that a short free-memory sample triggers reclaimBeforeSkip and a re-sample before the preload is skipped. The other checks that retained KV segments are released (parkedBytes == 0) when the preload is skipped. These tests exercise production behaviour that the supplied evidence does not show: StartupPreloader.reclaimBeforeSkip and currentRequiredGb, the retained KV segments, and segmentHostZeros.

Relevant threat T-041 (prefix cache, accepted risk SEC-035) and T-028 (residual GPU/KV data). Releasing retained segments on a short sample is plausibly neutral or positive for residual data. The production implementation was not in this batch, so I could not verify that segment retention or segment host-zeros handling keeps in-memory KV data from lingering, or that segments are scoped by cacheSalt. No security regression is evident from the tests alone. The next pass should review the production code for retained KV segment scoping and zeroing, and for the memory-reclaim logic, if it is in the PR. It should also check whether T-041 or T-028 need updating to mention retained KV segments.
